target_customer: Consumers who want to reduce phone use, via the Island app
problem: People want to cut screen time but friction based blockers are easy to bypass, so the studio uses a game that shows the result of choices.
business_model: Consumer app studio, subscription or in app revenue not stated
product_category: Consumer apps, screen time and habit building

founders.name: Ashish Selvaraj
education: Double degree in Computer Science and Business, University of Waterloo, 2025
founders.background_notes: YC page: delta live tables at Databricks and an infrastructure testing engine at Microsoft.

competitors.name: Opal
competitors.traction_then: Finalist in the 2025 Apple Design Awards social impact category

competitors.name: one sec
competitors.what: Adds a pause before opening distracting apps

competitors.name: Brick
competitors.what: Hardware puck that unlocks blocked apps

competitors.name: Apple Screen Time
competitors.what: Built in free iOS feature, easy to bypass

technical_complexity.rationale: Screen time apps on iOS rely on Apple's Screen Time APIs and a game layer, which is standard mobile engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Many similar apps exist and Apple controls the platform APIs, so the app can be copied quickly and depends on platform rules.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple ships a free Screen Time feature. No sourced incumbent action against Island.

market_need_then: Phone overuse is a widely discussed problem, and a crowded set of paid apps such as Opal sold at about $100 a year in 2026.

branding.domain_note: Uses appsidekit.com, not the exact word domain

identity.visual_style: Greetings from postcard motif across the site, farm theme in Island
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful, tagline Do things no one else will

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive site style exists but a search found other products called SideKit and Sidekick, and no outside press about the brand.

pivots.from: Third party directories describe SideKit as an iOS SDK for analytics and feature flags
pivots.to: Consumer app studio with the Island app, per the company site and YC page
pivots.why: Not stated. The company site still lists an SDK, so this may be a framing difference, not a pivot.

outcome_analysis: SideKit joined YC in Winter 2026 as a consumer app studio with two Waterloo graduates. It has no exit or failure and no verified funding. It competes with Apple's free Screen Time and paid apps such as Opal, with little defensibility beyond execution and retention in a game based approach. Early outcomes depend on Island's downloads, which no source reports.
notes: No funding information found beyond YC backing. Directories disagree on what SideKit does, calling it an iOS SDK, while the company site and YC page describe a consumer app studio with Island, so the pivot entry is uncertain. Google Play shows an app Island Screen Time Control under SideKit. Founders' founding location differs: YC lists Toronto, one directory lists San Francisco.
